evidence: Read all 27 criteria (2 gate, 16 functional, 5 polish, 4 visual). No criterion enumerates several requirements and then waives most of them: there is no 'at least N of', 'only X is required', 'minor issues acceptable' or similar relaxation anywhere in the criteria or prompts. Multi-part functional criteria (signin_and_client_scope, deleted_and_expired_messages, sent_once_in_order, search_and_transcript) each end with 'Both parts must hold; failing either fails this criterion' (e.g. functional/judge.toml:49,120,217,246), and the functional prompt sets one conjunctive bar: 'Every numbered leg and every sentence that names a step must hold ... A step you skipped ... fails the criterion' (scored/functional/prompt.md:26-28). Flow bundling is explicitly sanctioned by the skill's known-false-positive list (checks 26/28/33) and by the internal workbook annotation. Visual likert criteria each state one 5-anchor bar with descending anchors (visual/judge.toml:89-144). Instances reported (per 'Reports every instance'), none rising to a defect: (1) gates/render/judge.toml:25-35 deviates from the template's crisp 'Assign 1 only if every check holds; otherwise assign 0' (template gates/render/judge.toml:28) to 'This is a basic reachability/sign-in gate only. If the gate fails, assign 0; if the signed-in populated surface loads without any of the basic failures above, assign 1.' Together with render/prompt.md:10-11, which lists only blank page/generic error/unavailable server/static shell as failures, a judge could read 'basic failures' as reachability-only and treat the 'nothing private before sign-in' and 'incorrect password is rejected' checks as softer. Most natural reading still includes them ('above'); impact is bounded because the gate is zero-weight and both properties are re-graded in functional signin_and_client_scope (functional/judge.toml:44-45). (2) Several 'Fails if' summaries are narrower than the enumerated steps, e.g. signin_and_client_scope Part A positive list ('Pryce lease dispute' and 'Pryce will') not restated (judge.toml:44-45); wall_every_route item 3 'plain not-available' and item 1 positive list vs Fails-if only on leakage (:59-63); wall_added_live item 1 list disappearance 'within about ten seconds, without reloading' vs Fails-if 'keeps seeing M-13 messages' (:84,88); timer_changes '7 days beside the title' not restated (:130,135); safe_formatting 'opens in a new tab' vs 'simple formatting does not render' (:175,178). In the functional dimension these are resolved by prompt.md:26 (every sentence/step must hold), so the judge has one bar. (3) polish refusal_in_place (polish/judge.toml:62) states 'Then sign in with the right password: no reason is shown' but its Fails-if omits it, and the polish prompt has no every-step rule; practical impact is nil since a successful sign-in replaces the form. No runtime evidence is needed to judge this textual row; no judge run was used or claimed.
counterexample: Not a blocking counterexample: under a lenient reading of the render gate's 'basic failures above', an app that accepts a wrong password but otherwise renders could pass the zero-weight render gate; it would still fail functional signin_and_client_scope. A conforming app is not put at risk by any instance found.
suggested_fix: Optional: restore the template's closing sentence in gates/render/judge.toml ('Assign 1 only if every check holds; otherwise assign 0'), and make the narrower Fails-if summaries either complete or prefixed 'Also fails if any step above does not hold' (notably polish refusal_in_place).
